obligation: Bank recall of a misdirected wire (funds response)
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.211 (UCC Article 4A cancellation); FBI IC3 BEC guidance
trigger: Wire sent on fraudulent instructions (buyer wire in variant A; trust account disbursement in variant B)
deadline: Immediately on discovery. After the receiving bank accepts the payment order, cancellation needs that bank's agreement, so minutes matter
notify: Variant B: the company's escrow bank wire room (request recall and a hold harmless or indemnity letter). Variant A: the buyer calls their own bank; the company also alerts its bank and the receiving bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational; not a notification duty

obligation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) complaint
trigger: Any BEC attempt or loss; file regardless of the amount
deadline: As soon as possible (voluntary; no legal deadline). The FBI states IC3 may help banks and law enforcement freeze funds
notify: IC3 at www.ic3.gov with full banking details; the buyer files their own complaint in variant A

trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information without authorization (unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise) involving at least 500 consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery. Discovery is the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent (contractor sales associates included)
notify: FTC via the online form at ftc.gov (six content items in 314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more consumers; a single mailbox usually holds fewer, so count and document

trigger: A law enforcement official determines in writing that public disclosure would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still filed on time; the official may request that the FTC delay public disclosure for up to 30 days, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: State the determination and the official's contact in the FTC notice

trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information of Florida residents (for example name with Social Security, driver license, or passport number; or an email address with a password that permits access to an online account)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email (the compromised mailbox must not be used)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the FTC rule has no individual-notice procedure, so the federal deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) does not help here; confirm with counsel

obligation: Florida notice not required after a no-harm determination
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept for at least 5 years and provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for a mailbox that held no Social Security, ID, or account access data; counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay individual notice for the period stated in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination; 15 more days for individual notice if good cause is given in writing within the 30 days
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

obligation: Service provider breach notice to the company (inbound)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a); contract terms under 16 CFR 314.4(f)(2)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the transaction platform or closing software vendor) has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: Third-party agent must notify the company no later than 10 days after determination; contracts may set shorter times

trigger: Affected clients who reside outside Florida (about 30% of buyers)
notify: Residents and, where required, state attorneys general or regulators
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residency of every affected person

obligation: Florida Real Estate Commission notice of an escrow dispute
citation: Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(d)1.; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-10.032(1)
trigger: A diverted or missing earnest money deposit leads to conflicting demands on funds in the sales escrow account, or the broker has good-faith doubt about who is entitled to them
deadline: Written notice to the Commission within 15 business days of the last demand or of the doubt; start a settlement procedure within 30 business days
notify: Florida Real Estate Commission (Broker of Record)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the brokerage holds the deposit and demands conflict

citation: Title agency agreement and closing protection letter terms (contract)
trigger: Loss or suspected loss of funds from the title escrow trust account, or a claim by a buyer, seller, or lender
deadline: Per the agency agreement (treat as same day)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual not legal; confirm the contact by 2026-10-31 (P03 G-037)

trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
deadline: Per policy (typically as soon as practicable; call the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-26; a small brokerage is unlikely to meet the proposed criteria; recheck when final

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Considering an extortion or ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No for BEC; applies only if the incident turns into extortion

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: Within four business days after determining materiality

trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment found in a federal contract performance
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
